newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria c.bank buys marks to start currency board.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria c.bank buys marks to start currency board.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) has bought enough German marks on global markets to meet cash demand as part of preparations to launch a currency board system on July 1, the BNB governor said on Wednesday.
"We have enough marks to cover levs in circulation and meet retail demand from individuals and firms," Svetoslav Gavriiski told reporters.
The BNB will continue buying marks in the coming days until the currency board is introduced, he added.
Under the currency board system, designed to restore confidence in the shaky financial system, levs in circulation must be precisely matched by foreign exchange reserves.
Bulgaria chose the mark as anchor currency at a fixed exchange rate of 1,000 levs per mark.
The BNB board has yet to decide on the buy/sell exchange rates at its meeting on Thursday, said Gavriiski.
"Most likely the rates will be the same as voted by parliament - sell at 1,000 levs and buy at 995 per mark," he added.

Under the currency board system agreement with the International Monetary Fund, the BNB is also due to set up a counter to exchange cash levs for cash marks. Wholesale transactions will be conducted between and lev and mark accounts of the banks.

As part of pledges to free foreign exchange rules, the cabinet is expected to lift restrictions on buying foreign currency, said Gavriiski. So far Bulgarians were allowed to buy the equivalent of $2,000 annually.

Under the system, the BNB is committed to exchanging any amounts of its domestic monetary liabilities for marks. This commitment does not extend to other hard currencies, which banks will be able to buy freely on the market with marks.
